newsitem.title: USA: Oregon unemployment rate drops to 5.6 pct in April.
newsitem.headline: Oregon unemployment rate drops to 5.6 pct in April.

text.p: Oregon's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate declined two-tenths of a percentage point to 5.6 percent in April, the state's Employment Department said on Tuesday.
The drop puts Oregon's unemployment rate at the same level as in February, and slightly below the 5.9 percent 1996 annual average rate, the department said.
In April, 99,300 Oregonians were unemployed and 1,623,500 were employed.

"Any fears of an immediate slowdown in Oregon's economy should be eased by the April employment report," said David Cooke, an economist with the Employment Department. "The unemployment rate ticked back down and job growth was strong in services and manufacturing."
Total nonfarm payroll employment rose 6,400 jobs on a seasonally adjusted basis in April, the department said. The growth followed a decline of 1,800 jobs in March.
Job growth in the last 12 months has been 3.9 percent, and annualized growth over the past six months has been 3.4 percent, the department said.
In April, seasonally adjusted job gains were largest in services, construction and manufacturing.
